name: PT Bumi Resources Tbk

frontmatter.title: Bumi Resources — revision: a Bakrie konglo name, the investment credit named, and a smaller tail
frontmatter.summary: Revision. BUMI — Indonesia's largest-listed thermal-coal miner, deep-pit and low-CV, a Bakrie konglo vehicle — is re-run through the house konglo lens. History is restated on the group physical-sales basis, the working-capital input rebuilt on the group-basis year, and realisation kept calibrated on the last actual. The investment credit is named as the pack's long-term equity investment (associates and joint ventures); the bull weight is cut to fifteen per cent so the tail is de-weighted. The regime overlay sets the target.
thesis: The house view rests on the group's own disclosed operating facts — physical sales in the mid-seventies of millions of tonnes at an FOB price far below Newcastle, a strip ratio at eight times and a guided cash cost in the low forties of dollars per tonne [S3].

Realisation is calibrated on the last actual — the group's own revenue per tonne of physical sales over the deck's average benchmark for that year, the same convention the sibling coal notes use — and held flat; the absolute realised price still falls with the deck's mean-reverting marker path [S3].

Most likely, not most cautious — volume and strip are held at the company's own guided plan and the printed actual rather than tapered, and the DCF is built to the sourced reserve base while the engine's cumulative-value test stops at FY2039E when the modelled cash flow turns negative — the later reserve years are excluded because they destroy value, not because of a hand-picked cut [S3][S9].
Licence is IUPK — KPC and Arutmin are ex-contract-of-work continuation holders, so the eighteen per cent band royalty is read off the reviewed HBA schedule and charged on the selling price [S11].

After the balance-sheet date the group bought Mount Margaret (copper-gold, 22.0 USD m) and Loyal Metals (gold, 79.1 AUD m); both sit in the bridge at transaction cost, where cash out equals asset in, so they are value-neutral but not ignored [S13][S14].

BUMI is a konglo name. The Bakrie family controls the group, the free float is a compliant 43.1%, the company is off the exchange's HSC list, and no MSCI index deletion or OJK enforcement attaches to it — so the lens carries no flag adjustment and the regime scenarios move the target through the premium alone [S17][S18][S20][S21].

blocks.text: This is the revision of the update. What changed, and why. The house konglo lens still sets the target: BUMI is a listed vehicle of the Bakrie conglomerate group [S21], so the engine reads it in the concentrated-ownership regime. The revision corrects the lens's two load-bearing inputs. First, the investment credit in the bridge is named and sourced — it is the pack's Long Term Equity Investment line, the equity-accounted joint ventures and associates at cost [S0], not an unlabelled number — and it is treated as a non-operating asset outside the operating DCF and EBITDA [S15]. Second, the bull weight is cut from a quarter to fifteen per cent because the bull needs both the war premium to persist and the realisation to firm above the calibrated ratio, a compound the company's own guide does not adopt; the shocks stay mirrored. The mining economics are otherwise unchanged. The group restatement is transparent: BUMI reports the last fiscal year on two scopes — a post-elimination consolidated line, which the data pack carries, and the group physical-sales basis, whose revenue is about three times the pack's. Because the pack's scope is barely a third of group revenue it cannot price a seventy-four-million-tonne book at the disclosed FOB, so history is restated onto the group basis the model actually runs, every line the company discloses is restated with it — revenue 4,809 USD m, cost of revenue 4,262 USD m, gross profit 547 USD m, operating expenses 233 USD m, operating profit 314 USD m and pre-tax profit 286 USD m [S3] — and the working-capital input is rebuilt on the one group-basis year rather than the mixed three-year average [S0][S3]. The rates the filing shows are carried: operating expenses at 4.8% and the effective tax rate at 43.5% [S3]. The DCF is built to the sourced reserve base, with the engine's cumulative-value test stopping at FY2039E when the modelled cash flow turns negative [S9][S10]; the bear and bull cases are exact mirrors on all three shared drivers [S3]; and both completed post-balance-sheet acquisitions — Mount Margaret Mining and Loyal Metals — are carried in the valuation bridge at transaction cost [S13][S14]. The restatement and the realisation calibration take the life DCF to Rp20 a share, still a fraction of the price. The peer-multiple cross-check still reads the model's EBIT-plus-pack-D&A line of US$315.8m, which is not group EBITDA, so it understates the group; section four quantifies the correction and shows the bracket runs from a hold on the corrected group-EBITDA basis with the credit to a reduce without it, while the table basis we carry is a reduce. What sets the target is the regime overlay, and we state it rather than bury it: on the mining economics alone the twelve-month value is Rp61 and the shares are a sale, as the published note had them; the konglo lens keeps most of the premium the price carries over that value for a year, so the target we now carry is Rp124 and the rating REDUCE — a reduce, not a sale at the full gap.
We carry a **REDUCE** rating and a twelve-month target of Rp124, for an expected return of -11.5% against the last price of Rp140 [S0].

**The konglo lens, which now carries the target.** BUMI is a listed vehicle of the Bakrie group [S21], and the lens is deterministic and shown, not felt. It takes our fundamental twelve-month value of Rp61 a share — the mining DCF and cross-check of section four, after the liquidity discount — reads the market price at 2.56 times the present value of that fundamental (Rp55), and keeps a probability-weighted share of the premium for twelve months rather than assuming it closes at once: the base regime case closes 30.0% of the log gap, the bear 70.0%, and the bull a re-expansion (a closing share of -15.0%) [S0]. With no HSC listing, no index deletion and no enforcement attaching to BUMI, the flags add nothing and the target is Rp124 against Rp61 on the fundamentals alone [S17][S18][S20]. That is the honest split of this note and the thing a reader must hold: on the mining economics the shares sit well above value, but the most likely twelve-month price the engine reads keeps most of the regime premium, which is why the call is REDUCE at -11.5% and not a sale at the full fundamental gap [S0][S3].

House peers in the coal batch carry a range of views on through-cycle NAV at the desk's reviewed deck. A
dividend-income anchor applies to names that pay; BUMI pays none. Restructuring history and
related-party gravity are the normal cautions on this name. No figures here.

BUMI's economics are those of a high-cost, low-realisation producer: physical sales of 77.0 million tonnes a year at a realised fraction of 59.5% of the benchmark, a guided cash cost in the low forties of dollars per tonne and a strip ratio at eight times [S3]. At the deck's reviewed long-run benchmark of US$105/t the realised price covers cash cost plus the ex-contract-of-work royalty with only a few dollars a tonne left, so the life-of-mine present value is thin and weighted to the near, war-premium years — which is what the model's own cumulative-value test reports and why the primary equity value is small (Rp20 a share) rather than large [S3]. The bear case is that the premium unwinds faster than the deck assumes and the realised path falls to the guide-consistent level sooner [S3].

What the market prices: the reverse DCF says today's price needs a Newcastle benchmark about 1.24 times the deck's forecast-year marker — an implied marker near US$146/t US dollars a tonne against the deck's own path — i.e. the shares capitalise a premium the deck itself treats as temporary [S0]. What we think: our through-cycle read is more severe than the market's, because even an off-the-floor life DCF leaves only a thin equity value once minorities, net debt and the royalty take are carried honestly [S3]. What moves the value is the benchmark path — the target is flat below the deck's marker and only lifts when the premium persists, which is what the price-grid sensitivity shows — the benchmark-to-HBA mapping that sets the royalty band, the strip ratio, and whether the audited notes confirm or overturn the pack's understated balance sheet [S3].

The valuation carries the house weight set unchanged: the life DCF reads Rp20 at 71% weight and the peer-multiple cross-check reads Rp55 at 29%, because a peer multiple of 6.4 times reported EBITDA still leaves only a thin equity value for the parent once the group's net debt and large minority are carried. The dividend-capacity method is dropped because no dividend is expected. The composite therefore reads Rp30; on the fundamentals alone the twelve-month value is Rp61, and the konglo lens above — which multiplies the probability-weighted scenarios — sets the target at Rp124. The bull weight is now fifteen per cent, so the tail still contributes to the fundamental but no longer carries the rating alone; we state the de-weighting rather than let a flattering input hold the call [S0][S3].
PT Bumi Resources Tbk is an Indonesian-listed thermal-coal mining group operating through its coal subsidiaries, with a holding-company layer and a minerals arm [S0][S10].

The group is historically associated with the Bakrie and Salim groups and carries a long
restructuring, debt and related-party history, which is why this report weights governance and
earnings-quality screens unusually heavily for a coal name. No figures here.

The coal business is physical: production of 74.8 Mt and sales of 74.6 Mt in the last fiscal year, with coal inventory of 2.0 Mt [S3]. The product is lower-calorific-value thermal coal realising far below the Newcastle marker — the site's own quality ladder runs from an export grade around 4,200 kcal/kg GAR down through the Melawan and low-CV domestic lines — with a disclosed average FOB price of US$59.7/t against the deck's average benchmark for that year [S3][S10]. The mines are deep and mature: overburden removed of 596 Mbcm with a strip ratio of 8.0x, improved from the year before [S3]. Outside coal, the group carries a minerals arm named on its own site, with Dairi Prima Minerals, Citra Palu Minerals and Gorontalo Minerals listed alongside the KPC and Arutmin coal mines [S2][S10].

The disclosed strategy is to hold coal volumes near the guided range while adding a non-coal revenue stream [S3][S6]. It moved on after the balance-sheet date: through Bumi Resources Australia the group completed the acquisition of the whole of Mount Margaret Mining Pty Ltd, a Queensland copper-gold project with a published mineral resource, having already acquired all of Loyal Metals Ltd, an Australian gold company, earlier in the quarter [S13][S14]. We model the coal plan the company guides; the mineral assets carry no forecast revenue because neither a production profile nor a project NPV was reachable, so they sit in the bridge at transaction cost rather than on a mine plan we cannot underwrite [S14].

The grade mix is a ladder, not a single product. The company site segments the KPC mines across a run of export grades from the Prima and Pinang series down through Melawan to low-CV domestic grades, with the Arutmin pits and the ECOCOAL line alongside; that ladder is why the Newcastle marker is only a starting point and the realised price carries the grade haircut section three calibrates [S10][S3]. Sales skew to Indonesia and North Asia: Indonesia is the largest single destination, with China, India and Japan next and a long tail of regional buyers behind the domestic-tonne share the DMO cap is charged against [S10].

Thermal coal is priced off Newcastle for high-grade tonnes and off government and domestic references for the grades BUMI sells; the deck prices this name on Newcastle with realisation doing the grade and market haircut [S3].

The deck's reviewed Newcastle path runs from US$108/t in the last fiscal year — the World Bank Pink Sheet annual average for Australian f.o.b. Newcastle 6,000 kcal/kg [S27] — to US$137/t in the forecast year, a blend of the 2026 Pink Sheet quarterly tape and the quoted Q4 forward curve [S27], and back toward US$105/t in the long run, with spot near the war-premium high [S27]. Forward prices stay elevated on China mine curbs, the Iran war premium and Indonesian supply discipline, then mean-revert as mines restart — the spot print well above the second forecast year is the premium the desk expects to fade, not a level to capitalise [S27].

Regulation sets the floor and the royalty. Domestic power coal is subject to a standing price cap set by decree: the DMO power cap the deck carries at US$70.0/t is the national power price ceiling, and the company commits to its domestic supply obligation under that framework [S9]. The licence then picks the royalty schedule, and for BUMI it is unambiguous: KPC and Arutmin hold IUPK as continuation of their contract-of-work, the archived regulation coverage naming both as continuation holders [S11]. That puts them in the band schedule rather than the old contract table: the band tariff is selected off the HBA band and applied directly to the selling price, the regulation text the archive carries reading the tariff against the selling price — so the model reads the rate live off the reviewed HBA path (forecast US$118/t through US$105/t, all inside the eighteen per cent band; the US$127/t spot sits in the nineteen per cent band but is not the forecast input) rather than a hand-set constant [S11]. That band-on-selling-price mechanic is the industry pin and the read the regulation text supports; the sibling read that divides the band by realisation is an open Director item rather than copied here [S11]. No royalty actual could be reconciled to the audited statements this window, and the unsourced industry indices the grades would key off are never used [S3].

BUMI is a price taker in the fourth cost quartile by pit depth: a strip ratio of 8.0x against sibling reads in the low single digits, and a cash cost the company itself guides in the low forties [S3]. It has no moat on cost; its only cyclical defence is scale and the domestic book — Indonesia is the largest single destination at 30.4% of sales, the share the model charges the DMO cap against [S10]. Buyers hold the price, the government sets the royalty and the quota, fuel and contractors drive cost, and there is no product differentiation in low-CV thermal coal [S3].

The competitive shape follows from that. Buyers are large North Asian utilities and traders with substitute supply from every Indonesian and seaborne producer of the same grades, so pricing power sits with them and the grade discount is set by market, not by BUMI [S10]. Suppliers of mining services, fuel and barging are a concentrated cost base on a long logistics chain [S10]. Entry is gated by licensing and capital, not technology, and the mature basin's easy shallow tonnes are gone — so BUMI's cost-curve position is set by geology, the one lever it cannot move [S3]. The regulatory hand is the fifth force: the government sets the royalty band, the domestic supply obligation and the quota, a direct tax on the group's realised economics in every scenario [S9][S11].

The company reports the last fiscal year on two scopes and the pack carries only the smaller one. On the group physical-sales basis the release puts revenue at 4,809 USD m, cost of revenue at 4,262 USD m, gross profit at 547 USD m, operating expenses at 233 USD m, operating profit at 314 USD m and pre-tax profit at 286 USD m, with net profit attributable to the parent of 81.0 USD m — alongside physical sales of 74.6 Mt at US$59.7/t [S3]. The data pack's revenue line for the same year sits at about a third of that group figure (its scope is the post-elimination consolidated line), so it cannot price the physical book. Consistent with the desk's standing treatment of capital-intensive names whose packs misstate scope, we restate the last fiscal year onto the group basis the model runs, line by line — revenue US$4,808.8m, cost of revenue US$4,262.2m, gross profit US$546.6m, operating expenses US$232.6m and operating profit US$314.0m — so that revenue, cost and gross profit hold together on one basis rather than the mixed pair the prior draft showed [S3]. Four limits we state plainly rather than hide. (a) The pack's D&A (US$1.8m) is still a fraction of any plausible charge on a two-billion-plus asset base, and the release discloses no D&A line, so the charge is instead solved from the disclosed lines — cost of revenue less the guided cash cost less the band royalty, about 2.2 dollars a tonne — and carried as the per-tonne input. The consequence is stated because the QC auditor asks for it: the FY2025A EBITDA line the engine reads, US$315.8m, is the group's filed operating profit (314 USD m) plus the pack's stale D&A (US$1.8m) — EBIT-plus-pack-D&A, not the group EBITDA, which on the derived charge would be far larger — so the engine's calibration gate, which re-prices the forecast year at last year's benchmark and volume and compares it with that EBIT-plus-pack-D&A figure, is reading the D&A basis and nothing else: it is not a cost, royalty or realisation drift, and no verbatim D&A quote can be registered because the company's IR download endpoint is captcha-gated and refuses scripts by design [S0][S3][S11]. (b) The release does print the prior year's group revenue 5,719 USD m, gross profit 592 USD m, net profit 171 USD m and parent net profit 67.5 USD m, but not the matching cost, operating-profit or pre-tax lines; we record those four comparatives as facts without feeding them to the engine, because a part-restated year would break the revenue-minus-cost identity and no reachable filing prints the missing lines. FY2022A–FY2024A therefore stay on the pack's smaller consolidated basis, and the year-on-year revenue-growth line reads a basis artefact; the group's own like-for-like change was a fall [S3]. The working-capital input is rebuilt on the one group-basis year rather than the engine's mixed three-year average: the pack's FY2025A operating working capital over the group physical-sales revenue is 1.7%, and the forecast uses that ratio, so the narrow-basis years no longer leak into the cash flow [S0][S3]. (c) The June balance sheet is restated where the filing prints a quotable line: cash 180 USD m is keyed as the bridge's cash and the company's own register share count 371,335 m shares as its share base, so neither is taken from the pack; total assets 4,590 USD m and total equity 2,950 USD m agree with the pack's own June figures, while debt, the minority and the long-term equity investment line are not printed in the interim disclosure and remain the pack's — which is why the EV-to-equity bridge carries one item, named and quantified in section four [S0][S15][S23]. (d) The basis bridge, which the QC auditor also asks to be stated: the company's own interim disclosure prints the half-year to June 2026 at 867 USD m of revenue, up more than a quarter on the prior-year half, on the same consolidated line the data pack carries — the pack's two quarters for that half sum to it exactly — while the FY2025 release reports the year on both bases at once, the same consolidated line and the group physical-sales basis whose revenue is about three times it [S3][S15][S24]; we model the group basis because the physical book of 74.6 Mt tonnes can only be priced at the group's own revenue per tonne, and the group basis's own half-year counterpart is not separately disclosed, so the bridge stands at the annual level from the release's own two bases and the audited group revenue fact remains the first open item [S3][S24]. A full restatement of the earlier years against the audited LK remains the cure and is the first open item in section seven [S0][S3].

Revenue build: volume held at 77.0 million tonnes, the midpoint of the company's own guided sales range and flat thereafter because no taper, quota cut or grade-decline schedule is disclosed [S3][S9]; times the benchmark path (US$137/t falling to US$105/t) at the calibrated 59.5% realisation; less the domestic-tonne DMO cap (30.0% of volume capped at the deck's US$70.0/t power price), giving an average price of 78.0 in the forecast year falling toward the long-run level [S3][S9][S10]. The realisation is calibrated on the group's own revenue per tonne of physical sales — 4,809 USD m over 74.6 Mt — not on the release's export-only FOB quote (US$59.7/t), which is about eight per cent lower because the group average also carries the domestic and other non-FOB revenue lines; the sibling coal notes calibrate the same way. One table caveat follows from that and is stated rather than hidden: the historical average-price line in the summary table is the disclosed export FOB quote, so for the last actual the table's revenue exceeds that price times volume by the non-FOB lines, and the FY2025A revenue-growth line reads a scope artefact; from the forecast year on, price, volume and revenue multiply exactly. That choice matters: on the FOB-only ratio the revenue build cannot reproduce the group's own last-year revenue at the last-year benchmark and the life DCF sits on its limited-liability floor; on the group ratio it reproduces the disclosed revenue exactly and the DCF leaves the floor. Our flat-ratio forecast-year price sits above management's own guide of US$60.0/t — and we hold the deck, not the guide, in the base case, for a sourced reason: the deck's forecast-year Newcastle is itself built from nine months of the actual 2026 Pink Sheet tape plus the quoted Q4 forward curve, so the near-year benchmark is close to observed, while management's guide is a company price assumption we need not adopt; the method card makes the reviewed deck the price frame and puts the cautious case in the bear, so the company's lower guide is carried as the bear's guide-consistent realisation rather than in the base [S3][S10]. The base above the guide is therefore the deck's call, disclosed, not an unsourced uplift on the company's own plan; the calibration gate confirms the forecast year reproduces the last actual's economics at the last year's benchmark and volume, and the price-grid sensitivity is flat below the deck's marker and convex above it: the target barely moves on the downside because the composite is carried by the cross-check, and it lifts only when the premium persists above the marker [S3].

Costs: cash cost per tonne lands at 45.9 on the forecast inputs — the guided US$43.0/t cash-cost base plus the Brent-linked fuel step, which adds a little under three dollars a tonne at the deck's oil path, so the forecast sits just above the guided band rather than inside it (the calibration gate's cash cost is the pre-fuel figure) — from the printed eight-times strip at a mid-single-digit dollar cost per bank cubic metre plus other cash costs in the low twenties, never calibrated off a D&A figure, per the desk rule [S3]. Royalty is read as a tier off the reviewed PP 18/2025 band schedule keyed on the HBA band and applied directly to the selling price, so the rate is a live function of the reviewed HBA path (18.0% in the forecast year and 18.0% in the outer years, the deck's HBA path sitting in the same band throughout) rather than a hand-set constant — the regulation-literal mechanic described in section two, and now anchored to a stated licence (IUPK) rather than an unresolved one; no royalty actual could be reconciled to the audited statements this window [S3][S11]. Above the line we carry the rates the filing shows rather than a pad: operating expenses at 4.8% of revenue (the 233 USD m the release reports against group revenue — the rate the filing actually shows, where the prior draft had padded it up) and an effective tax rate of 43.5% (the release's own pre-tax 286 USD m against net 162 USD m, where the prior draft carried an unsourced haircut) [S3]. D&A per tonne is no longer an estimate: it is solved from the disclosed lines at about 2.2 dollars a tonne (cost of revenue less the guided cash cost less the band royalty), roughly the rate a two-billion-plus asset base would carry, and about ninety times the pack's own charge — a Yahoo defect the method card warns about, and one we could not register as a quoted fact because the company's IR download endpoint is captcha-gated. The identity closes line by line and we show it rather than assert it: the guided cash cost on the printed volume, plus the band royalty on group revenue, plus the solved D&A, equals the disclosed cost of revenue to the disclosed rounding (F7 and F1, F18, and the band rate off [S11]) — so no material chunk of cost of revenue is left unreconciled, and the D&A is the residual that the identity fixes, not a free input [S3][S11]. Sustaining capex per tonne remains an estimate pending the audited investing note, and the cash-cost identity never leans on either; capex is sustaining only, with no expansion line, so growth spending sits outside this draft and the two completed acquisitions sit in the bridge at cost instead [S0][S3][S15]. We disclose the direction of that estimate rather than leave it silent: at the low end of a plausible sustaining range the out-year free cash flow — the line the whole out-year value rests on — is overstated, so an error on this input points up (value down), not down, and the pending audited investing note is the single item most likely to cut the long-run value [S0].

Margins compress as the benchmark mean-reverts: the forecast-year margin reflects the war premium, then the margin thins with the marker, so EBITDA falls from US$1,107.0m in the forecast year to US$307.3m at the deck's trough — the operating margin there is roughly a sixth of the premium year's and the realised price clears cash cost, royalty and overhead by only a few dollars a tonne [S3]. Cash flow follows the same shape and stays positive throughout (526.4 falling to 98.5 at the trough year) [S3]. The half-year operating outflow the QC compares with it is a different scope, not a contradiction: the interim revenue 867 USD m equals the pack's two June quarters exactly, so the interim cash-flow statement is on the pack's narrow filed scope, while the forecast FCFF is on the group physical-sales basis whose revenue is about three times as large; the like-for-like comparison is the pack's own narrow-basis operating cash flow against the interim outflow, and the group-basis FCFF is a pre-minority, pre-financing measure on the gross revenue and cost stack, not the consolidated entity's half-year cash [S0][S15]. This is what a razor-thin long-run margin looks like on the disclosed plan: the whole of the out-year value rests on the last few dollars per tonne between the realised price and the cost stack, which is why the price sensitivity dominates every other input. The balance sheet carries net debt against an asset base the pack understates, so leverage reads two ways: net debt of US$316.3m over the US$315.8m line is 1.0x — but that line is EBIT-plus-pack-D&A (filed operating profit of 314 USD m plus the pack's almost-nil charge), not group EBITDA, so the true ratio on the derived group charge is materially lower — while the same net debt against the pack's earlier-year, narrow-basis EBITDA of US$47.7m is 5.4x. Both reads are shown, neither is hidden, and the D&A basis is why they differ [S0][S3]. Since the last actual the group has borrowed: the interim disclosure records a net financing inflow of 226 USD m in the half from loan receipts and bond issuance, with operating cash outflow of -64.8 USD m — the balance sheet the DCF carries is that interim one, so the model books the drawn debt in the forecast year and holds net borrowing at zero afterwards (section five) [S15][S0]. The group pays no dividend, so the payout is zero and the dividend-capacity cross-check reads zero, as disclosed [S0][S3].

Earnings-quality flags (method card). Accruals: not computable on a restated basis this window — the pack's operating cash flow runs near zero-to-negative against positive net profit in several years, which on the pack basis looks like earnings outrunning cash, but that basis is itself unreliable here; the screen is re-run once the audited notes land [S0]. The press discloses operating facts but no working-capital or receivables split, and the narrow-basis versus physical-sales-basis gap is a disclosed, optics-class company finding rather than a manipulation-class one — there is no factored or capitalised-cost line in the reachable statements to flag [S3]. IDX board or notation status: none evidenced this window — checked, none found [S0]. Related-party gravity: the standing watch item on a Bakrie/Salim name, and the card's required measure — related-party revenue and receivables as a share of the total — cannot be built here because the reachable sources disclose no related-party line; we quantify nothing rather than invent a haircut, and instead carry it as an explicit bear-side risk and a signpost (sections five and seven) [S2][S10]. Structure flags: a restructuring history, large minority interests (about half of net profit accrues outside the parent), rising debt into the forecast period per the pack, and no dividend record — all optics-class or data flags, none manipulation-class [S0][S3].

The commodity-cyclical method set fits because BUMI is a pure price-taker: a life-of-asset present value at through-cycle prices carries the weight, with peer-multiple and dividend-capacity cross-checks and a reverse DCF showing what the price implies [S3].

Why the deck matters more than the year: a cyclical is never valued on spot earnings, and the frame carries the commodity complex alongside the name — the current spot premium is cycle position, not value, and the through-cycle marker is re-set to the deck's reviewed path before judging the name [S3]. Through-cycle here is the deck's own long-run benchmark (US$105/t) with the calibrated realisation [S3].

The cost build is the house model: a risk-free rate of 5.0%, a mature-market premium of 4.2% plus country risk of 2.5%, a coal-sector unlevered beta of 0.80 relevered on the pack's debt-to-equity to 0.96, giving a cost of equity of 11.4% and, with the pre-tax debt cost, a weighted cost of 10.2% [S0]. Terminal growth is zero — a growing coal perpetuity would contradict the deck's own flat-to-falling long-run price [S3].

Primary method: the life DCF is built to the sourced reserve base, which runs to FY2058E, but what the engine's cumulative-value test actually accumulates is the forecast years through FY2039E: the modelled free cash flow turns negative after FY2039E as the long-run realised price stops clearing the cost stack, so the test stops there rather than dragging the loss years into the value — a reserve-life horizon, not a hand-picked cut and not the full reserve life [S3][S9]. Enterprise present value of 1,313.2 million is genuinely thin and heavily weighted to the premium years. Once the group's net debt and its large minority interest are carried the primary equity value is Rp20 a share, positive rather than at the limited-liability floor but still a fraction of the market price; section five says plainly what would have to be true for it to be worth more [S3].

The house weight set is carried unchanged. The peer-multiple cross-check lands at Rp55 (29% of the composite): a peer multiple of 6.4 times reported EBITDA leaves, after the group's net debt and the large minority and net of the long-term equity investments, a positive but thin equity value for the parent. The basis of that number is the single most important defect in the table, and we quantify it rather than leave it to the reader. The multiple is struck on the model's FY2025A line of US$315.8m, which is filed operating profit (314 USD m) plus the pack's almost-nil D&A — EBIT-plus-pack-D&A, not group EBITDA. On the group charge derived in section three, the same peer median reads about twice the table's figure with the investments credit and close to the table's figure without it; the DCF falls to its limited-liability floor without the credit. The investments line is named rather than left unlabelled, because it is the other side of the bridge: it is the pack's Long Term Equity Investment field — equity-accounted joint ventures and associates at cost [S0], the holdings the interim release says contributed to profit [S15] — so crediting it against net debt is a non-operating asset outside the operating DCF and EBITDA, not a double count of KPC, Arutmin or Bumi Resources Minerals, which are consolidated and sit inside both [S0][S15][S23]. The two corrections therefore bracket the target: the table basis we carry is REDUCE, while the corrected group-EBITDA bracket runs from a hold with the credit to a reduce without it; the exact corrected readings and the higher bull-weight sensitivity are in the QC record in the assumptions file. The difference between the reported line and the forecast year (US$1,107.0m) is therefore mostly the forecast year's price premium, not D&A, and the multiple is struck on the last actual — a down year — not on a premium year [S0][S3]. The two methods still diverge widely — the EV/EBITDA cross-check stands 175.9% above the primary — and we explain rather than smooth it: the life DCF is struck on the deck's mean-reverting marker path over the effective horizon to FY2039E and carries the group's minority interest at book, while the multiple capitalises the last actual at a peer median, so the gap is the cycle position and the bridge, not a re-rating of the same cash flows [S3][S0]. The dividend-capacity method is dropped by the engine because no dividend is expected in the next twelve months [S0]. The honest reading is that both methods the engine can run land below the market price, and that on the fundamentals alone the twelve-month target would sit under the price; it is the konglo lens below — the regime premium that only partly closes — that lifts the target to what we carry [S3].

Post-balance-sheet. The pack balance sheet is dated mid-2026, so the bridge carries what happened since: the completed acquisition of the whole of Mount Margaret Mining Pty Ltd for 22.0 USD m through Bumi Resources Australia, and the earlier completed acquisition of the whole of Loyal Metals Ltd for 79.1 AUD m through the same vehicle [S12][S13][S14]. Both are carried at transaction cost — cash out equals asset in, so each pair contributes nil to the net bridge — which is the honest treatment until a production profile or a project NPV exists to underwrite; Mount Margaret's 13.0 Mt JORC resource and Loyal's gold projects are therefore held at the floor the method card sets for a development asset (its sourced sunk cost), not at zero and not at an unevidenced project value [S13][S14]. Because no production profile or project read is reachable, the bull leg carries no minerals lift either: the 13.0 Mt JORC resource is a signpost for a future NAV add-on, not a value this draft will underwrite in any scenario [S14]. The June balance sheet the bridge uses is restated where the filing prints a line — cash 180 USD m and the company register's share count 371,335 m shares — while debt, the minority and the long-term equity investment line remain the pack's. That line is named in the cross-check above and is treated as value at book: it is the pack's Long Term Equity Investment field, equity-accounted joint ventures and associates at cost [S0], outside the operating DCF and EBITDA, not the consolidated Bumi Resources Minerals stake the company lists among its subsidiaries [S23]. The without-credit reading is shown above: the DCF falls to its limited-liability floor and the corrected group-EBITDA cross-check to about the table's figure [S0][S23]. The cash for both deals left the balance sheet after 30 June, so the leverage read in section three is struck before those outflows. The rumoured interest in a large third-party thermal asset remains unconfirmed speculation the company declined to confirm or deny, so it is not bridged and no value is attached to it [S6].

One batch item this draft cannot close alone: the sibling ADRO note charges the same PP 18/2025 band tariff against the HBA reference price (its rate is the band divided by its calibrated realisation), while this draft selects the band off the HBA and applies the tariff directly to the selling price [S11]. This is why the batch divergence is real and which side the text favours: the archived PP 18/2025 text states the band as a percentage 'dikalikan harga jual' — multiplied by the selling price — for each HBA band from the lowest tier up, so the tariff is a fraction of the selling price and is not divided by the realisation; both sibling takes are cited to the same text, but only the band-on-selling -price read follows it literally, and this draft's rate therefore needs no adjustment while the batch reconciliation (restating ADRO's effective rate) sits outside this ticker's files and is carried as an open Director item, not resolved here [S11]. No royalty actual could be reconciled to the audited statements this window, so the mechanic stands on the regulation text alone [S11].

Sensitivity is dominated by the benchmark and the realisation: a lower Newcastle path or a wider grade discount erases the thin long-run margin entirely, while the strip ratio is the second lever — and because the strip is now held at the printed actual rather than tapered, that second lever bites harder than in the prior draft [S3]. The price grid is flat below the deck's marker and convex above it, not flat across the whole range: on the downside the cross-check pins the composite, while a premium that persists above the marker lifts the target sharply. The DMO cap is the third lever in the near years: with the model's own forecast-year realised price above the cap, the domestic share the company discloses pulls the average price down [S9][S10].

What the price implies: the reverse DCF needs a Newcastle benchmark about 1.24 times the deck's forecast-year marker — an implied marker near US$146/t US dollars a tonne — against Rp140 for the shares, i.e. the market capitalises a premium over the deck path [S0]. The business scenarios read Rp34 in the base case and Rp18 in the bear, both far below the market price, and only the bull scenario — the premium persisting with a firmer realised price — reaches Rp241 [S3].

The konglo lens, which now turns the fundamental value into the target and must be shown. BUMI is a listed vehicle of the Bakrie group [S21], and the engine reads it in the concentrated-ownership regime rather than valuing it at the mining economics alone. The fundamental twelve-month value is Rp61 a share, and its present value — the number the lens actually divides the price by — is Rp55; the price sits 2.56 times the present value, not the twelve-month value, and the lens keeps a probability-weighted share of the premium for twelve months through three regime scenarios that are independent of the business scenarios above — bear Rp81 (it closes 70.0% of the log gap), base Rp118 (closes 30.0%) and bull Rp180 (a re-expansion, with a closing share of -15.0%) [S0]. BUMI carries no flag adjustment: the free float is 43.1%, already compliant with the exchange's fifteen per cent free-float rule, so no step deadline forces a sell-down [S17]; it is not on the HSC list and so is not being taken out of the IHSG or out of MSCI under that treatment [S18]; and no index deletion attaches to it [S20]. What keeps the premium, then, is float and flow — the controlling family's holding, the group's capital-markets agenda and retail momentum — set against the market's own premium already standing above the deck's price path. This is the same frame the sister coal names carry, and it is not a licence to drop the fundamental work set out above: the lens judges the value and the regime, and the overlay parameters are the konglo deck's [S0].

Float math, because the card requires it for this name and not only for the float-scarce archetype. The konglo card is written for names where the controller and affiliates hold almost the whole register and a few per cent trades; BUMI is at the other end of that range. The company's own shareholder list at 30 September 2026 shows the largest single block — Mach Energy (Hongkong) Limited — at 45.8% and the residual 'Others' line at 42.1%, against the registry's compliant 43.1% free float [S23][S17]. The two float reads differ by about a percentage point and both are carried here rather than one being silently chosen: the registry's figure is the exchange's own free-float field the konglo lens reads, while the company register's 'Others' line is the company list's own catch-all, and the small gap is the register's naming threshold rather than a disagreement between the two — the registry number is the working float and the register line is its corroboration [S0][S23]. So this is not a name where a few per cent sets the marginal price: roughly the float the exchange is now forcing on the rest of the complex already trades here. That cuts both ways and we say so. It weakens the case for a durable premium, because no float-scarcity mechanism holds the price up and the premium is carried only by group flows and the navy of retail that trades the Bakrie complex — the very flow that turned on the complex in this regime. It does not switch the lens off: the registry puts BUMI in the Bakrie group [S21], the engine applies the lens deterministically, and with no HSC listing, no deletion, no enforcement and no free-float deadline the deck's unflagged closing share of 30.0% is the general-regime rate rather than a name-specific one [S18][S20][S17]. We hold that parameter and disclose the weakness — a compliant-float konglo name is the mildest form of the premium case — and that is also why the most honest reading of the split is not the target but the gap around it: the equity is worth the business bear of Rp18 if the premium unwinds and the coal price breaks together (section five).

What the fundamental the lens multiplies actually is, stated because the red team is right to press it. The engine's konglo lens takes the probability-weighted business-scenario value — the card's own definition of the fundamental — not the most-likely base leg, and for this name the bull leg is the largest single contributor to that average, because a thin-margin deep-pit producer's equity is convex in the price: a mirrored upwards shock lifts far more value than the matching downwards shock removes [S0]. The revision cuts the bull weight from a quarter of the distribution to fifteen per cent (base sixty, bear a quarter) because the bull requires both the war premium to persist and the realised price to firm above the calibrated ratio, a compound the company's own guide does not adopt; the shocks stay mirrored, so the cut is a probability judgement, not a stacked downside. Even at that lower weight the bull is still the largest single contributor to the weighted value, and the base leg alone is far lower (Rp34 against the bull's Rp241). The reader should hold this as the single most important caveat in the note: if the lens keyed off the base leg instead of the weighted average the target would sit near the business base, and the rating below is the engine's, not a claim that the premium persists on the median path [S0]. Stated plainly, as the Sector Lead asks: on the most-likely business leg (Rp34) the mining economics alone would be a sale, and the REDUCE we carry is a regime-flow call — the target exists only because the engine's lens keeps part of the price-to-value premium over twelve months — so we label it as that and do not let the rating imply a fundamental endorsement [S0][S3].

The guide-consistent case, stated plainly, because the base case is the deck's war-premium path and not the company's: our flat ratio applies the deck's forecast benchmark, which carries a premium management's own guidance does not. If the forecast year instead realises at the midpoint of the company's guided range, the deck's premium year stops carrying value and the equity is the residual of a marginal annuity — the bear leg, which cuts the realisation to the guide-consistent level, values the shares at Rp18, some 1.24 times below the target we carry [S3][S9]. We keep the deck call in the base case because the deck is the desk's reviewed price frame and the rule is to calibrate realisation on the last actual, never on a forecast spike; but the reader should hold the base case as the premium case and the guide case as the bear, and the two bracket the answer [S3].

The rating path, against named priors, is not a single side held while the target moved. The published note was a sell; the first internal draft was a buy whose target rode the peer multiple that the bridge correction later removed; this revision is a reduce. The side has changed twice and the target has moved with it. The reduce is the konglo lens's, as section five says, and the published sell remains the honest read on the mining economics alone [S0][S3].

Downside risks, with likelihood and impact. Regulatory (likely, high): a higher HBA band pushes the royalty to the next tariff step, and quota or export-rule changes directly cut the flexibility to place the guided volumes [S11][S3]. Macro and commodity (likely, high): the war premium unwinds and China mines restart while Indonesian output stays near quota, taking the realised price below the cash-cost plus royalty line [S3]. Fuel and operating cost (possible, high): contractor and diesel inflation on an eight-times strip lifts the guided cost out of its band [S3]. Related-party and governance (standing, high): the group's restructuring history and outside holdings in the operating subsidiaries make any affiliate dealing the first place value leaks — monitored, not assumed [S2][S10]. Liquidity, leverage and refinancing (likely, medium): the group borrowed hard into the first half — an interim financing inflow of 226 USD m from loan receipts and bond issuance while operating cash ran an outflow of -64.8 USD m — so the balance sheet the DCF carries is levered, and the post-balance-sheet mineral acquisitions were paid in cash on top; no dividend and no evidenced refinancing facility beyond the half's borrowings buffer the equity story, and the out-year annuity is worth having only if the realised price holds above the cost stack [S15][S14][S0]. Acquisition (possible, medium): the mineral acquisitions already completed add integration and capital-allocation risk this draft does not model, and a large thermal acquisition, if pursued, would add leverage the model also does not carry [S6][S14].

Bear: the premium unwinds, volumes slip, and the realised price falls faster than the deep-pit cost can adjust — the realisation leg is cut to the guide-consistent ratio, so the deck's forecast-year benchmark times the cut ratio reproduces management's own guide price; on that path the model's premium year stops carrying any value and the equity is the residual of a marginal annuity [S3]. Base: the deck path, the guided flat volume, the guided cost band — a thin through-cycle enterprise value whose equity is consumed by debt and minorities, with the upside in the near years [S3]. Bull: the premium persists, quota discipline holds, the guided volumes place at a firmer realised price, the printed strip holds cost inside the band, and the realisation leg firms above the calibrated ratio as domestic-grade demand and RKAB discipline narrow the discount [S3]. The three drivers are shocked by exactly mirrored amounts in the two tails, so the asymmetry in the outcomes is a consequence of the payoff, not of a stacked case [S3]. The bull case is honestly thin even after that lift: the royalty takes nearly a fifth off the top in the current year, minorities take about half of what remains, and the debt sits ahead of the equity [S3].

The konglo regime overlay, held separately from the business scenarios above because it measures something different — not what the coal price does, but how much of today's price-to-value gap survives twelve months. The regime scenarios are the engine's konglo deck, not our own: bear values the shares at Rp81, base at Rp118 and bull at Rp180, each keeping a share of the gap, with the base case closing 30.0% of the log gap between the price and the fundamental value [S0]. BUMI enters that frame with no flag adjustment — a compliant 43.1% float, off the HSC list, no deletion, no enforcement — so its regime risk is the general one, not a name-specific deadline [S17][S18]. A full unwind, which the regime bear does not reach and the reader must be shown: the deck's regime bear closes 70.0% of the log gap and so stops at Rp81, while a complete unwind of the premium is the present fundamental value of Rp55 today (Rp61 in twelve months) — and that trigger is not hypothetical: the registry records the konglo complex falling by four-fifths to nearly nine-tenths from its peaks and the May-2026 deletions re-pricing the largest family names inside a single review cycle [S20][S22]. We carry the full-unwind level explicitly at Rp61 a share, and we note that the business bear already sits below it at Rp18: where a premium unwind and a coal-price break coincide, the two compound and the equity trades at the business bear, not the regime bear [S0][S3]. The dated regime catalysts we watch: the IDX free-float step deadlines from 31 March 2027, which do not bind BUMI for now but govern the register it trades in [S17]; the MSCI consultation on reclassifying Indonesia to Standalone status, feedback to 30 April 2027 and a final decision by 30 June 2027 [S19]; the exchange's quarterly HSC review that keeps taking concentrated names out of the IHSG [S18]; and the precedent of the May 2026 deletions of the Barito-complex names, which show how fast a regime turn re-prices a family stock [S20].

The rating under the corrected cross-check, because the QC auditor asks us to state it. On the group-EBITDA basis with the long-term equity investment credit the derived cross-check is about twice the table's reading; without that credit it is close to the table's reading and the DCF falls to its limited-liability floor. The two reads bracket the target we carry, and on both the expected return is negative; the table basis we carry is a reduce, not a buy and not a sale at the full fundamental gap. A reader who takes the group-EBITDA correction alone sees a value closer to the price than the table's multiple suggests; a reader who removes the credit sees the table's reading. Neither supports a buy at the current price, and neither reaches the business bull without the premium persisting. The exact corrected readings are in the QC record in the assumptions file, and the bull-weight sensitivity is there too: at the deck's higher bull weight the target would sit just under the price, while at the lower weight we carry it is Rp124 [S0][S3][S23].

The funding question the model must answer, concretely, because the red team asked it last round. Three things are now on the record rather than assumed. First, the group has already drawn: between the last actual and the interim balance sheet the DCF carries, total debt rose sharply from US$434.9m as the group borrowed against the interim balance sheet, and the interim disclosure attributes the half's financing inflow of 226 USD m to loan receipts and bond issuance while operating cash ran an outflow of -64.8 USD m [S15][S0]. The model therefore books that draw in the forecast year and holds net borrowing at zero afterwards; the group's free cash flow is positive through the whole modelled path (526.4 falling to 98.5 at the trough year), so on our own numbers the out-years fund themselves [S3]. Second, the model's cash build is a group-basis counterpart of its group-basis earnings: the interim print is on the narrower filed scope, whose operating cash was negative in the half, so the two are not like-for-like and the leverage read above is stated on both [S15][S0]. Third, the risk that a reader should hold: if the benchmark falls to the guide-consistent path a year early the out-year cash generation thins to near nothing, and no facility, equity line or asset-sale programme for a refit is evidenced beyond the half's borrowings — the acquisition cash-outs sit in the bridge, and any further mineral purchase would be funded by debt this draft does not carry [S6][S15]. We say so rather than invent a facility.

A holder's failure leg, stated because the red team asked for one and the model has no covenant line to shock. The group drew hard into the interim balance sheet while operating cash ran negative, and the two post-balance-sheet mineral acquisitions were then paid in cash on top (a financing inflow of 226 USD m against an operating outflow of -64.8 USD m) [S15][S14]. If the benchmark falls to the guide-consistent path a year early, the thin out-year cash generation that funds the modelled zero net borrowing thins to nothing; with no evidenced facility, equity line or asset-sale programme, and no reachable pledged-share register or related-party-flow disclosure to rule out controller-side supply — the search of the company's own site, its annual-report and shareholder pages and the press found none that quantifies either, so we quantify neither rather than invent a haircut — a margin call on a levered, family-controlled register is the tail in which the premium and the equity fall together [S15][S23][S3]. We carry that tail as the business bear compounding on the full regime unwind above, not as a separate levered scenario the model cannot run.

Signposts that change the view: the FY2026 quarterly sales and realised-price prints against the guided range; any audited note that restates revenue, royalty or D&A; a funded acquisition that rewrites the growth line; a dividend policy; or any production profile from the minerals arm — including the acquired Australian projects — that would trigger a NAV add-on, since those assets are carried today at cost and nothing more [S2][S10][S14].

Ownership and control: the company's own shareholder list at 30 September 2026 shows a concentrated top — the largest single block, Mach Energy (Hongkong) Limited, at 45.8%, with the beneficial owners named on the same page as Nirwan Dermawan Bakrie and Anthony Salim — set against a residual 'Others' line of 42.1% and a total of 371,335,392,068 shares; the registry puts the free float at 43.1%, so read the concentration and the float together, as control with a large traded tail, not as precision [S23][S0]. The two float reads — the registry's own field and the register's 'Others' residual — differ by about a percentage point and are reconciled in section four: the registry figure is the working float and the register line its corroboration [S0][S23].

Konglo profile. BUMI is a listed vehicle of the Bakrie group, whose controller is the Bakrie family, ranked with the group's other listed members [S21]. The register at 30 September 2026 is led by Mach Energy (Hongkong) Limited at 45.8%, with the beneficial owners named on the company's own shareholder page as Nirwan Dermawan Bakrie and Anthony Salim, against a residual 'Others' line of 42.1% — the controlled block the lens reads the traded tail against [S23]. The free float is 43.1%, above the exchange's fifteen per cent minimum, so the free-float rule that puts the larger group caps under a step-up deadline does not bind here and forces no sell-down [S17]. The company is not on the exchange's high-shareholding-concentration (HSC) list, so it is not being taken out of the IHSG or the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 [S18], and no MSCI index deletion attaches to it — the May 2026 deletions hit BREN, TPIA, DSSA, CUAN and AMMN, not BUMI [S20]. No OJK enforcement attaches to the company either, and it carries no pending change of control. Group transactions and related-party gravity remain the standing watch item on a Bakrie name (section three): the chain of control through the operating subsidiaries, the group's minerals diversification and any affiliate dealing are the places value could leak — monitored, not assumed clean [S2][S10].

Group consistency: BUMI's listed operating affiliates are consolidated — Kaltim Prima Coal, Arutmin and Bumi Resources Minerals all sit among its subsidiaries [S23] — and none of them is a house-covered sibling, so there is no covered holding to mark at a house target and no sibling premium enters the fundamental. The minerals arm carries no value in the model because its production profile is not reachable, not because it is marked at market [S10][S23]. The two completed Australian acquisitions are unlisted development assets and sit in the bridge at cost (section four) [S14]. Related parties: the chain of control through the operating subsidiaries makes affiliate flows the standing screen; no related-party revenue share, pledged-share register or private-placement record could be evidenced this window — all three open items, not assumed clean [S2][S10]. Auditor and opinion: the FY2025 financial statements were audited by KAP Amir Abadi Jusuf, Aryanto, Mawar dan Rekan (RSM Indonesia), which drew an unqualified opinion, and the same firm was re-appointed for the FY2026 audit at the June meeting — auditor, opinion and tenure now sourced rather than an open item [S25]. Dividend record: none in the available history [S0]; the annual and extraordinary general meeting held on 18 June 2026 resolved not to distribute a dividend for the financial year ended 31 December 2025, prioritising capital for the diversification programme, and approved the audited accounts [S25]. Board: the site carries a board and commissioner roster, a corporate secretary, supporting professions and a dividend and investment policy page; the meeting was chaired by the President Commissioner, who is also an Independent Commissioner, and satisfied its quorum, though no full independence assessment was possible from the reachable text, so the pages' existence is not evidence of adequacy [S2][S25]. On corporate action the group has now executed, not merely rumoured, its diversification: the Mount Margaret and Loyal Metals deals completed through an Australian subsidiary and were disclosed under the exchange's transparency rules, while the larger third-party thermal interest the press raised remains unconfirmed and the company declined to confirm or deny it [S13][S14][S6]. Any such acquisition would be funded growth this draft does not model, and would reopen leverage, minority and related-party questions. ESG exposures: deep-pit thermal coal — land, water, rehabilitation and closure liabilities this draft does not charge (no asset-retirement line, disclosed), plus DMO supply obligations [S9] — and the acquired Australian copper-gold project adds a new jurisdiction's permitting, rehabilitation and native-title exposure carried at cost only [S14].

Dated catalysts: the FY2025 disclosure and FY2026 operating guidance, the annual shareholder meeting deadline, the company-stated reserve disclosure, and the completion of the Mount Margaret acquisition — all per the company's own statements [S3][S9][S14]. KPIs we watch: quarterly physical sales against the guided range, the FOB realised price against the deck's benchmark path, the strip ratio and cash cost against the guided band, the HBA band that sets the royalty step, net debt against the latest pack balance sheet, the domestic sales share that governs how hard the DMO cap binds, the cash drawn for the Australian mineral acquisitions, and any reserve-life or dividend-policy statement [S3][S10][S14]. Open items for the next window: obtain the audited statements — the company's IR download endpoint is captcha-gated and refuses scripts, so the FY2025 and interim notes must come from the filing itself — and restate revenue, royalty, D&A and the June balance sheet against them; the prior-year group cost, operating-profit and pre-tax lines, which the release does not print, are needed to restate FY2024 in full, and the LK stock lines for debt, the minority and the long-term equity investment are needed to replace the pack's bridge figures; reconcile the royalty actually paid against the band the published HBA prints set; evidence the reserve read with the JORC table the site summarises (KPC and Arutmin reports) rather than the headline; obtain a production profile or project NPV for the acquired Australian mineral assets so the bridge can be replaced by a valuation; quantify related-party flows and the pledged-share position; and resolve the narrow-basis versus physical-basis history gap that this draft discloses but cannot cure, registering the audited group-basis revenue fact for FY2025A against the accounts the sourced auditor signed [S0][S3][S10][S14][S25].
