assumptions.basis: CALIBRATED ON THE LAST ACTUAL, per the round-1 desk rule and the sibling convention (AADI calibrates the same way, on revenue over sales volume). FY2025A realised price is the group's own revenue per tonne of physical sales: group revenue US$4,808.8m (S3/F6) over coal sales 74.6 Mt (S3/F1) = US$64.46/t, against the coal deck's FY2025A Newcastle average of US$108.4/t (the deck's own reviewed series, cited in the report through the deck.coal.newc.FY2025A placeholder), so the realised ratio to the benchmark that prices this name is 64.46/108.4 = 0.5946 — held across the forecast, NOT fitted to the FY2026E Newcastle spike (the deck's FY2026E 137.0 is a war-premium print the desk expects to mean-revert; a ratio fitted to it would carry a trough realised price into the long run). We calibrate on the group revenue per tonne rather than the release's FOB quote (US$59.7/t, S3/F3) because the FOB line prices only the export book: the group's disclosed average per tonne is US$4.76 higher (about US$355m of domestic/non-FOB revenue lines between them), and an FOB-only ratio left the model unable to reproduce the group's own revenue at the last year's benchmark and volume (the engine's calibration gate read -36% on EBITDA). Using the group average puts history and forecast on one basis: at the FY2025A benchmark and volume the revenue build reproduces the disclosed US$4,808.8m. BUMI realises a large discount to Newcastle because its product is lower-CV thermal coal (KPC 4,200 GAR is the low end of the product ladder, S10/F17) sold partly into the HBA/DMO-anchored domestic market. The RATIO is held flat; the ABSOLUTE realised price still falls with the deck's mean-reverting marker path (FY2026E ~81.5 before the DMO cap, down to lt ~62.4 US$/t). Our flat-ratio FY2026E ASP sits above management's own FY2026E guide of US$60-62/t (S3/F9) precisely because the deck's FY2026E benchmark carries a war premium management's guide does not adopt; the difference is disclosed in sections three and four, the bear scenario carries the guide-consistent path, and the price-grid sensitivity is flat below the deck's marker and convex above it (not flat across the whole +/-20% range, per QC N2). Because the reviewed ICI drivers are needs_source (deck coal.ici3/ici4), the realisation lever is calibrated to the REVIEWED Newcastle deck; HBA is used only for the royalty band and the DMO cap.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: Set at 0.30 from the company's own customer disclosure, replacing the engine 0.0 that reasoned off the guided ASP: the company's business-info page shows Indonesia as the single largest sales destination at 30.4% of FY2024 coal sales (S10/F15, "Data as of December 2024"), so domestic tonnes are material and the US$70/t DMO power cap can bind. BUMI further states it supplies a quarter of the national DMO (S9), confirming domestic-power placement. We apply the cap to the whole Indonesia-destination share as a proxy for domestic tonnes (the power-only split is not disclosed), which slightly over-applies the cap since not every domestic tonne is a power tonne; within the model's own ASP path the FY2026E realised price sits above the cap, so the cap binds and pulls the realised price down, the conservative direction for this name. The cap stops biting once the deck's benchmark mean-reverts and realised prices fall below the cap.

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: FY2025A actual strip ratio was 8.0x (S3/F4; overburden 596.2 Mbcm, F5), improved from 8.7x the year before. BUMI works deep, mature pits, so we HOLD the last actual 8.0x flat across the forecast and the long run: no company forward strip or mine-plan schedule is disclosed in any reachable source, and the method card forbids modelling strip-ratio drift without a sourced mine plan, so holding the disclosed actual is the most-likely read in both directions. The overburden volume is the physical companion: 596.2 Mbcm removed on 74.6 Mt sold is the 8.0x the company reports (S3/F5).

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: Solved to land total cash cost inside management's FY2026E guide of US$43-44/t (S3/F7): with strip 8.0x, 8.0 x 2.6 = 20.8 plus other cash costs 22.5 = 43.3 US$/t before the fuel-price adjustment (fuel_share 0.3 on brent). The 2.6 US$/bcm sits below the sibling AADI/DSSA reads (3.0-3.2) because BUMI's deeper pits spread fixed mining overhead over more bcm per tonne; the check is the per-tonne cash cost, which is the company's own guided number, never a D&A-derived figure. Cash cost = COGS minus royalty minus D&A is respected: the model's unit_cost excludes both.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Solved jointly with cost_per_bcm to the guided US$43-44/t cash cost (S3/F7): 8.0 x 2.6 + 22.5 = 43.3 US$/t before fuel adjustment. Covers hauling, barging, crushing, port and marketing on BUMI's long KPC/Arutmin logistics chains.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: SUPERSEDED — retained only as the flat-regime record; the model runs tier mode, so the engine reads the band rate live from the deck's reviewed schedule coal.royalty_iupk keyed on d.coal.hba (0.18 across the deck's FY2026E-lt HBA path, all in the 70-120 band) and applies it DIRECTLY to the selling price, per the archived regulation text in the coal deck (fund record evidence on royalty_iupk from PP No. 18/2025, S15/S35: the band tariff multiplied by the SELLING price, so no division by realisation). The near-year step that tiering gives (0.18) deliberately does NOT adopt the current HBA spot band (0.19): the band now tracks the same reviewed deck series the price path keys off, so the model's royalty and revenue read the same frame. The sibling ADRO band-divided-by-realisation flat read diverges from the archived text and from this pinned tier mechanism and is left as an open Director item — see §4. BUMI's KPC and Arutmin are ex-PKP2B IUPK-continuation holders in scope of that schedule. The FY2025 press release discloses no royalty line to reconcile against, so no LK-actual check was possible this window — an open item in section 3.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: DERIVED FROM THE DISCLOSED LINES (C7); the audited LK notes remain unobtainable (the company's IR download endpoint is captcha-gated, so no verbatim D&A quote could be registered). The charge is solved from the group income statement the model now runs: D&A = COGS US$4,262.2m (S3/F18) less cash cost (guided US$43.3/t x 74.6 Mt, S3/F7 and S3/F1) less the 18% IUPK band royalty on the selling price (0.18 x US$4,808.8m, S11) = about US$167m, i.e. 2.24 US$/t on 74.6 Mt. That is ~8% of the group's US$2.1bn fixed-asset base, a plausible mining charge, and it is 90x the pack's US$1.8m (S0) — the known-understated Yahoo read of a direct-method LK the method card warns about. Using 2.24 rather than the prior draft's unsourced 2.5 removes an invented cushion and ties D&A to the disclosed statements. The cash-cost identity above never calibrates off this figure (cash cost = COGS minus royalty minus D&A), but the calibration gate's actual EBITDA is struck before a correct D&A charge because a `da` fact cannot be quoted from any reachable source — the reason its residual gap is disclosed rather than closed.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: ESTIMATE, OPEN ITEM (C7): set at 2.0 US$/t (~US$150m a year on ~75 Mt), a maintenance level for KPC/Arutmin fleet replacement and mine development on mature pits. No company-disclosed sustaining-capex figure was reachable this window (the group release carries no capex line, S3); the pending LK investing-cash-flow note will pin this down. No expansion capex is modelled (capex_other zero), so the two completed Australian acquisitions sit in the bridge at cost rather than as a growth line in the cash flow.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: REBUILT ON FY2025A ONLY (QC F3), not the engine default average of FY2023A-FY2025A, which mixed the narrow pack years with the group-basis year the model now runs. The pack's FY2025A operating working capital of US$80.8m (current assets less cash less current liabilities plus current debt, S0) over the group physical-sales revenue of US$4,808.8m (S3/F6) is 1.68%; the model's nwc line is revenue times this ratio, so it reproduces the pack's balance-sheet working capital on the revenue scope the model actually runs rather than tripling a narrow-basis balance. The earlier FY2024A and FY2023A pack years are not restated (the release prints no group cost lines for FY2024A), so using them in a three-year average would import the scope artefact into the forecast; one group-basis year is the cleanest available anchor and the basis is stated.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Set at 0.435, the LK-implied effective rate on the group physical-sales basis the model now runs: the company's FY2025 release discloses PBT US$286.1m (F22) and net profit US$161.8m (F23), i.e. a 43.4% effective charge (Indonesian corporate tax plus the withholding/branch charges on the operating subsidiaries). The prior draft's 0.40 haircut is removed per round 1 (C5): a 3.5pp understatement on thin trough margins flatters every positive year with no source. The engine default averages the pack's narrow-basis years and is not used.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Not the engine default this round. The pack's June-2026 balance sheet puts total debt at US$732.99m against US$434.88m at the FY2025 year end, so about US$298m of debt was drawn between the last actual and the interim balance sheet the valuation bridge uses; the interim disclosure corroborates it with a net financing inflow of US$226.14m in the half from loan receipts and bond issuance (S15/F30) while operating cash ran negative (S15/F29). We book that draw in FY2026E so the model's debt path agrees with the balance sheet the DCF carries, and hold net borrowing at zero thereafter: no further facility, equity line or asset-sale programme is evidenced for the outer years, and the model's own free cash flow is positive through the whole forecast (see section five for what would fund the out-years if it were not). The interim balance sheet precedes both Australian acquisitions, whose cash-out sits in the bridge instead.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Set at 0.50. The engine default (0.43) averages the pack's narrow-basis years, but the company's FY2025 press release on the physical basis discloses net profit US$161.8m with US$81.0m attributable to the parent (S3/F10), i.e. minorities take ~50% — consistent with the group's structure (large outside holdings in KPC alongside BUMI's control, and a 30% outside interest in Arutmin). Rounding to one half is the honest read of the disclosed split.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Set at 0.0. BUMI has paid no dividend in the available price history (the pack records zero dividends and the press release discloses no distribution), and the group is still rebuilding its balance sheet after the long restructuring while funding minerals diversification; no payout is the conservative and evidenced base case. The div_yield cross-check reads zero accordingly.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set at 0.0. For a thermal-coal producer the long-run real growth of the residual annuity is nil; the same 0.0 the sibling ADRO, BYAN and DSSA drafts carry. A 2% house terminal rate would capitalise a growing coal perpetuity the deck's own flat-to-falling long-run price path contradicts.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Set at 0.048, the rate the LK shows being paid on the group basis the model runs. The FY2025 release discloses operating expenses US$232.6m (F20) against group revenue US$4,808.8m (F6), i.e. 4.8%; the prior draft's 6% pad for an unquantified holding-company layer is removed per round 1 (C6) — an unsourced conservatism that depressed value. Clamps inside the template's [0, 0.5].

challenges.challenge: The report states the bear and bull shock "exactly mirrored amounts", but fund record shows the realisation shock is bear x0.8 versus bull x1.25 — not mirrored — and that unmirrored 25% lift is what drives the bull leg to fpv 244.8 (vs base 29.1), i.e. the bull supplies ~68 of the 89 fundamental the konglo lens multiplies. A one-sided, unsourced realisation lift is the single input carrying the target.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The bull's realisation shock is now x1.2, the exact mirror of the bear's x0.8 — the same twenty per cent each way — so the three shared drivers are mirrors, as §5 claims, and the asymmetry that remains in the leg values is the payoff's convexity, not a stacked shock. The mirror cut the bull leg from a 271 twelve-month value to 239 and the fundamental the lens multiplies from 88 to 80, the direction the challenge wanted. We also corrected the §5 wording and recorded why the residual convexity is left in the model rather than smoothed away.

challenges.challenge: Base-case FY2026E ASP is 78.02 (model line) against management's own guided US$60-62/t (F9) — ~26% above the company's plan, worse than the 73.75 the prior round already flagged as ~21% high. MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE anchors the base case on the company's plan; here the deck's war-premium path is the base and the company's own guide is demoted to the bear.
challenges.answer: Rebutted with evidence, with a clarifying change. The base uses the desk's reviewed Newcastle deck, not a deviation from the company plan: per the deck basis the forecast-year marker is built from nine months of actual 2026 Pink Sheet tape (Q1 122.3, Q2 135.4, Q3 138.1) plus the quoted Q4 forward curve, so the near-year benchmark is close to observed, while management's US-62 guide is the company's own price assumption. MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE makes the reviewed deck the price frame and places caution in the bear, which is exactly where the guide-consistent realisation sits — so a base above the guide is the deck's call, disclosed, not an unsourced uplift. The calibration gate confirms the forecast year reproduces the last actual's economics at the last year's benchmark and volume, and the FY2026E ASP gap carries little out-year value because the long-run ASP is the deck's mean-reverting marker. §3 now states the source of the near-year benchmark and the deck-versus-guide split explicitly.

challenges.challenge: The konglo premium_ratio is struck against a "fundamental 12-month value" of 89 that is the probability-weighted business scenarios, ~75% of which comes from the 273 bull leg; the most-likely base is 32 and the composite 29. The lens therefore multiplies a bull-dominated average, and the 25% weight on a leg that is ~8.4x the base is the heroic input.
challenges.answer: Accepted in part; the construction is the engine's and is now explained rather than hidden. The konglo lens takes the probability-weighted business-scenario twelve-month value as the fundamental (VAL_KONGLO_REGIME section 2 defines the fundamental as the business scenarios), not the base leg, and for this thin-margin deep-pit name the bull is the largest contributor because equity is convex in the price — a mirrored upward shock adds far more value than the matching downward shock removes. This revision cuts the bull weight to 0.15 (base 0.60, bear 0.25) because the bull needs both the war premium to persist and the realisation to firm above the calibrated ratio, a compound the company's own FY2026 guide does not adopt; the shocks stay mirrored, so the cut is a probability judgement, not a stacked downside. Section 4 states the convexity, names the base and bull legs, gives the reduced-weight target, and tells the reader the target would sit near the business base if the lens keyed off the base case.

challenges.challenge: The konglo lens is built for float-scarce names (controller 80-99%, a few percent traded), but BUMI's free float is 43.11% (registry S2) and the controller's actual stake is never stated. §4 gives no float math for why only 30% of the gap closes for THIS name, which the konglo card explicitly requires.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The register is now sourced and the float math for THIS name is written. The company's own shareholder list at 30 September 2026 puts the largest single block, Mach Energy (Hongkong) Limited, at 45.78% (F33/S23), with the beneficial owners named on the same page as Nirwan Dermawan Bakrie and Anthony Salim, against a residual 'Others' line of 42.09% (F34) and the registry's compliant 43.11% free float. §4 argues the closing share from it: a compliant float means no scarcity mechanism holds the premium and no free-float deadline bites, so the premium rests only on group flows — the mildest form of the konglo case. We hold the deck's unflagged 0.30 because the registry puts BUMI in the Bakrie group and the lens applies deterministically, and the report discloses that weakness.

challenges.challenge: No scenario reaches the full premium unwind. The regime bear stops at 106 (closes 70% of the log gap) while the fundamental value is 89; the report's own registry facts — konglo stocks -80-89% from their peaks (S9) and the May-2026 deletions of BREN/TPIA/DSSA/CUAN/AMMN (S20) — show the tail exists but it is not carried anywhere.
challenges.answer: Accepted. §5 now carries the full unwind explicitly: the deck's regime bear closes 70% of the log gap and stops at 104, while a complete unwind is the fundamental itself at 88 — and the trigger is the registry's own precedent (the konglo complex down as much as nine-tenths from its peaks, S20/S22). We state the full-unwind level and note that the business bear (18) already sits below it, so a premium unwind coinciding with a coal-price break lands at the business bear, not the regime bear.

challenges.challenge: Pledged shares, the controller's stake and related-party flow are all admitted open items with no bear leg, on a name carrying a Bakrie restructuring history; and the leverage leg has no failure case despite debt +298m into H1-2026 with operating cash -64.83m (F29) and no evidenced refinancing (F30).
challenges.answer: Accepted. We state the search and its result: the company site, its annual-report and shareholder pages and the press were searched and disclose no pledged-share register and no related-party-flow line, so we quantify neither rather than invent a haircut. We add the failure leg as a stated holder's state, not a shock the model cannot run: the group drew hard into the interim balance sheet while operating cash ran negative and then paid two cash acquisitions on top (financing inflow 226.14 against operating outflow 64.83, F29/F30), so if the benchmark falls to the guide-consistent path a year early the thin out-year cash thins to nothing, and a margin call on a levered family register is the tail in which the premium and the equity fall together — carried as the business bear compounding on the regime unwind.

challenges.challenge: capex_unit is an unsourced estimate at 2.0 US$/t (~US$150m/yr), held flat across the forecast for a 74.6Mt deep-pit mature producer — a low maintenance number that inflates free cash flow. It is disclosed as an open item but the direction of the bias (up) is not examined.
challenges.answer: Accepted in part. No audited sustaining-capex figure is reachable this window (the group release carries no capex line and the IR download endpoint is captcha-gated), so the input stays an estimate; §3 now states the direction of the bias rather than leaving it silent — at the low end of a plausible sustaining range the out-year free cash flow, the line the whole out-year value rests on, is overstated, so an error here points up (value down), and the audited investing note is flagged as the item most likely to cut the long-run value.

challenges.challenge: The two completed Australian mineral acquisitions (Mount Margaret, 13Mt Cu-Au resource, S14; Loyal Metals gold, S14) are carried at transaction cost in every leg, so the bull leg adds no minerals NAV even though the card allows at least sunk cost plus any sourced upside.
challenges.answer: Accepted with the reason stated. Both completed acquisitions are held at their sourced sunk cost (the method card's floor for a development asset), not zero; §4 now says explicitly that because neither has a reachable production profile or project NPV, the bull leg carries no minerals lift either, and the 13 Mt JORC resource is a signpost for a future NAV add-on, not a value this draft will underwrite in any scenario.

challenges.challenge: QC's calibration.ebitda gap is +52.6% (model 481.8 vs actual 315.8), dismissed as a D&A artefact, but the solved D&A (~2.2 $/t) plus guided cash cost (43.3 x 74.6 = 3,230) does not reconcile COGS 4,262.2 (F18) — leaving a large unexplained chunk of cost of revenue.
challenges.answer: Rebutted with the arithmetic, which closes. Cost of revenue 4,262.2 (F18) = guided cash cost 43.3 x 74.6 Mt = 3,230.2 (F7/F1) + the 18% band royalty on group revenue 4,808.8 = 865.6 (S11) + a D&A residual of 166.4 (2.23/t). The D&A residual is about 8% of the group's ~US.1bn fixed-asset base, plausible for a mining charge, and the calibration gate's 'actual' EBITDA (315.8) is struck before a correct D&A only because no da fact can be quoted (the IR endpoint is captcha-gated). So no large chunk of cost of revenue is unexplained; the residual is the D&A the engine cannot restate as a quoted fact. §3 now shows the line-by-line identity rather than asserting it.

challenges.challenge: BUMI carries zero konglo flags (compliant 43.11% float, off the HSC list, no deletion, no enforcement), and the card says the closing share c rises with the name's flags — so the unflagged case is the one where the premium persists longest. Yet the bull regime leg only re-expands -15% and the base still closes 30%; no challenge is offered for the possibility that an unflagged premium closes less, which is the bull side of the same mechanism.
challenges.answer: Accepted as an argument rather than a parameter change. The deck sets the unflagged closing share and we cannot move it, but §4 and §5 now argue why 0.30 is the deck's general-regime rate for an unflagged name rather than a name-specific one: with no HSC listing, no deletion, no enforcement and no free-float deadline there is no forcing event inside the window, and the same compliant float that gives no scarcity mechanism also gives no sell-down catalyst — so 0.30 stands and the bull regime leg keeps its re-expansion. The report discloses that a lower closing share is the natural bull for an unflagged name.

challenges.challenge: The royalty mechanic diverges within the batch: this draft charges the 18% band on the selling price while the sibling ADRO note divides the band by realisation, both cited to S11, and it is left as an open Director item rather than reconciled.
challenges.answer: Rebutted with the regulation text. The archived PP 18/2025 text states each band as a percentage 'dikalikan harga jual' — multiplied by the selling price — so the tariff is a fraction of the selling price and is not divided by the realisation; both sibling takes cite the same text, but only the band-on-selling-price read follows it literally, so this draft's rate needs no adjustment and the batch fix (restating ADRO's effective rate) sits outside this ticker's files as an open Director item. §4 now quotes the text's own phrasing to make the justification explicit. No royalty actual could be reconciled to the audited statements this window, so the mechanic stands on the text alone.

challenges.challenge: The HOLD exists only on the konglo lens. On the mining economics the previous (published) note was a SELL: the fundamental twelve-month value is Rp80 against the Rp140 price and the Rp131 target comes from the lens keeping roughly two-thirds of the premium. But the lens multiplies a "fundamental" that is about 75% the 25%-probability bull leg (business scenarios base Rp31 / bear Rp18 / bull Rp239, weighted Rp80), so the rating turns on a tail, not on the most-likely path. BUMI also carries NO regime flags - free float 43.11% (compliant), off the HSC list, no index deletion, no enforcement - so the konglo card premise (controller and affiliates hold 80-99%, a few percent trades, float sets the marginal price) does not hold for THIS name, and the deck's unflagged closing share is what preserves most of the premium. The most-likely twelve-month path for this name is therefore not established.
challenges.answer: Accepted, and answered on both legs the Lead names. The most-likely twelve-month path is now stated explicitly in §4: on the base business leg the mining economics alone would be a sale (the base leg reads Rp34), the lens multiplies the probability-weighted average (Rp61 after the bull de-weighting), and the target we carry (Rp124) exists only because the engine's overlay keeps part of the price-to-value premium over twelve months; §4 labels the REDUCE a regime-flow call that the mining economics do not support. On the flags: §4 and §5 argue from the float math why the deck's unflagged closing share (0.30) is the general-regime rate for a compliant, flagless name — no HSC listing, no deletion, no enforcement, no free-float deadline, so no forcing event sits inside the window, and the register's own float (registry field beside the company list's "Others" residual, S0/S23/F33/F34) leaves no scarcity mechanism to hold a premium up. The weakness is disclosed rather than smoothed. The revision keeps the scenarios' mirrored shocks but cuts the bull weight to 0.15 (base 0.60, bear 0.25) because the bull needs both the war premium to persist and the realisation to firm above the calibrated ratio, a compound the company's guide does not adopt; the report states the caveat that a base-leg lens would sit near the business base. Round two adds the corrected cross-check on group EBITDA and names the investment credit as the pack's long-term equity investment (equity-accounted JVs and associates), so the fundamental is no longer carried by an unlabelled item; the base business leg remains far below the price and the regime-call label stands. No input moved toward the price.

challenges.challenge: The fundamental the lens multiplies is not source-clean. The two inputs most able to move the thin out-year value - da_unit US$2.24/t and capex_unit US$2.0/t - are derived or estimated with NO audited LK and no verbatim quote (the IR endpoint is captcha-gated; the group release carries no D&A/capex line), and the whole FY2025A income statement is restated 3.38x onto a press-release table. The QC leaves this open on the record: Q1 FIX (restatement basis and its comparability with the covered peers, which carry their packs un-restated) and Q2 FIX (history and forecast D&A sit on different bases, so the model's FY2025A EBITDA line of US$315.8m is EBIT-plus-pack-D&A, not the ~US$480m group EBITDA, and the +52.6% calibration gap is an artefact the model itself created).
challenges.answer: Accepted in the part the record allows and stated plainly where it does not. (1) The two load-bearing inputs: no audited LK is reachable — the company's IR download endpoint is captcha-gated and refuses scripts by design, so no verbatim D&A or sustaining-capex quote can be registered; da_unit stays derived from the disclosed lines (cost of revenue less the guided cash cost less the band royalty) and capex_unit stays a stated estimate, and §3 now names the direction of the capex estimate's bias (up: the out-year FCF, and so the value, is overstated at the low end). (2) The ONE D&A basis: §3 now states that the FY2025A EBITDA line the engine reads is the filed group EBIT plus the pack's stale D&A — EBIT-plus-pack-D&A, not group EBITDA — and that the calibration gap is that basis and nothing else; the cure (a quoted da fact) needs the LK. (3) The restatement basis, reconciled with the comparison set and disclosed: the peers carry their packs un-restated because their packs are already the group line, while BUMI's pack is the same consolidated line the company prints for its interims (H1-2026 revenue, S15/S24) and the FY2025 release additionally gives the group physical-sales basis the model runs; §3 now carries that bridge and the audited group-basis revenue fact is the first open item. Round two restates the June balance-sheet cash and share count from the filing, records the FY2024 group comparatives the release prints (revenue, gross profit, net profit, parent net profit) without feeding a part-restated year to the engine, and quantifies the corrected group-EBITDA cross-check; the audited LK cost lines and D&A remain unobtainable, which we state rather than bridge. No input moved toward the price.

The gate's 'actual' is EBIT US$314.0m (S3/F21) plus the pack's D&A of only US$1.8m (S0), i.e. US$315.8m, because no `da` fact can be quoted: the audited LK notes are captcha-gated (the company's IR download endpoint requires reCAPTCHA, so the tool refuses it by design) and the release discloses no D&A line. The group's own D&A, solved from COGS US$4,262.2m (S3/F18) less cash cost (S3/F7, S3/F1) less royalty, is about US$166.4m, so group EBITDA is about US$480.4m and on that charge the like-for-like gap is under 1%. The fact schema requires a verbatim quote containing the value, so the derived figure cannot be registered as a `da` fact (QC B1's first route is barred); we instead quantify the effect on the load-bearing cross-check, as B1's fallback requires. On group EBITDA of US$480.4m the 6.44x peer median gives (6.44 x 480.4 - net debt 553.3 - minority 1,285.9 + investments 935.1) = US$2,188.7m / 371.335bn shares x 18,125 = about Rp106 a share, not the table's Rp54.5, lifting the composite and the twelve-month fundamental and target with it. Without the credit the group-EBITDA cross-check reads about Rp61 a share and the DCF falls to its limited-liability floor; with it the corrected cross-check is about Rp106. The two readings bracket the target: on the corrected group-EBITDA basis the with-credit twelve-month target is about Rp130 (HOLD) and the without-credit target about Rp118 (REDUCE), while the table basis we carry is REDUCE at about Rp124 under the 60/25/15 base/bear/bull weights; at the deck's 25% bull weight the table target would be about Rp132 (HOLD), the sensitivity the QC C3/L1 challenge asks to see.
